FACTUAL 2 - was spot sampled at an intraday high? Run 1 argued yes and tilted the median down for spike-fade; Run 3's finer data shows the high was $81,731 at ~20:00Z and price had already eased to ~$81,186 by 22:49Z. Run 3 is right: roughly 0.7% of the fade has already occurred, which removes most of Run 1's justification for centering below spot. FACTUAL 3 - NFP inside the window: all three agree the August Employment Situation prints 2026-09-04 12:30Z, inside the window. Settled, and it argues for width, not direction. FACTUAL 4 - instrument precision: Run 3 flagged a ~1% reconciliation gap between the question background's Aug 21 close ($77,378) and CoinGecko's own 00:00Z snapshots. Real but small and unresolvable here; it is a further argument against a narrow band, not a shift. JUDGMENT - dispersion. Run 3's 6,900 leans on an 18-session SD of ~3.0% that is inflated by including the Aug 19-22 breakout jumps; its own ex-breakout figure is ~1.9%. Runs 1/2 at ~5,100 sit at sigma ~2.45%, essentially the unconditional trailing-30d number, which under-weights that today was itself a 5.4% session (volatility clusters) and that a top-tier macro print lands mid-window. Neither side is right: I land at sigma ~2.8%, above Runs 1/2 and below Run 3, giving 5,900. JUDGMENT - drift: no evidence breaks the tie between momentum and squeeze give-back, and at a one-day horizon the martingale is the bet I would take, so the median is spot with a token -0.05% and asymmetric tails. All three runs declined escape mass and I agree - the required one-day moves (-32% / +23%) have no mechanism in play.
